speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are a neonate presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after birth. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if your mother had a fever during pregnancy or delivery, or if you were born prematurely?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a 31-week preterm infant with chorioamnionitis and seizures strongly suggests neonatal sepsis or hypoxic-ischemic injury. REQUEST TEST: Blood Culture, Gram Stain, CBC, and CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: Cranial Ultrasound.
